task: Make release-unit materialization resumable when persisted execution already points at a canonical superseding branch and main advances again.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Live bounded rehearsal replay on trusted Release Unit Execution #144 (run 37609591473) failed after all source gates passed with RELEASE_UNIT_PRIOR_MATERIALIZATION_BRANCH_MISMATCH. Persisted U01 already records branchRef release-unit/dev-control-plane-multi-unit-rehearsal-v1-u01-supersede-a96074891ce8-ab2e09fcc439a199. Fresh AUTHORIZE reprojects executionTransaction and resets branchRef to the root canonical release-unit/dev-control-plane-multi-unit-rehearsal-v1-u01. reconcileMaterializationBranch then inspects/compares the root branch while requiring priorExecution.branchRef to equal it, so a valid previously superseded lineage cannot be resumed when main advances again.
observableOutcomes: A persisted STALE release unit whose executionTransaction.branchRef is a previously validated superseding branch can be resumed without editing persisted state.
The runtime validates the actual persisted prior branch against the prior manifest before allowing any further supersession.
The next branch remains deterministic from the stable root canonical branch plus fresh target-base/binding identity rather than recursively growing supersede suffixes.
An existing exact next superseding branch is reused idempotently; no duplicate branch, PR or merge is produced.
Missing, noncanonical, moved, wrong-tree, wrong-base or wrong-identity prior branches remain fail-closed with direct machine-readable errors.
The unchanged U01 rehearsal proceeds beyond RELEASE_UNIT_PRIOR_MATERIALIZATION_BRANCH_MISMATCH after merge.
unresolvedRisks: Trusting persisted branchRef without reconstructing and validating the prior materialization could authorize foreign branch state.
Using the prior superseding branch as the naming root could create unbounded nested supersede branch names and unstable identities.
Inspecting only the root canonical branch can confuse older materialization with the persisted branch actually referenced by state.
Retry logic must not force-push, delete or mutate an existing branch.
executionTransaction supersedes metadata must identify the branch actually superseded, not merely the root canonical branch.

in: Separate the stable canonical naming root from the persisted prior materialization branch during reconciliation.
Inspect and validate priorExecution.executionTransaction.branchRef when it differs from the root canonical branch.
Derive the next deterministic superseding branch from the stable canonical root and fresh manifest identity.
Preserve the actual prior branch in supersedes receipts/transaction metadata.
Add adversarial regression coverage for supersede-of-supersede resume and fail-closed prior-branch drift.
Replay the same immutable rehearsal source after merge.
out: No manual edit of control-plane/release-state branches.
No force push, branch deletion, PR rebasing or receipt fabrication.
No relaxation of remote branch base/tree/message/binding validation.
No change to release-unit material intent, source provenance or risk thresholds.
No Template Factory, Builder, storefront, database, auth, payment or inventory work.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This path decides whether a persisted child release branch is trusted and whether a successor materialization may be created. A false PASS could merge foreign code; a false BLOCK breaks resumability, so branch lineage and identity require critical-practical proof.

acceptanceCriteria: When priorExecution.branchRef already names a canonical superseding branch, reconciliation validates that exact remote against the prior manifest instead of rejecting it solely because it differs from the root canonical branch.
The next superseding branch is derived from the stable root canonical branch and fresh targetBaseSha/bindingDigest.
The supersedes receipt records the actual persisted prior branch and head.
Retrying against an already-created exact next superseding branch reuses it without push.
A missing or noncanonical persisted prior branch fails closed and does not silently push fresh materialization over another identity.
Exact-head CI, Completion Truth and Lifecycle Closure pass before merge, then the immutable rehearsal source is replayed.
invariants: Persisted release-state remains the authority for which prior materialization branch must be validated.
The root canonical branch remains the deterministic naming root for future supersessions.
Remote branch base, tree, commit message, manifest and binding identity remain fail-closed.
No existing branch is force-updated or deleted.
A retry must not create duplicate PRs or merges.

failureModes: AUTHORIZE resets branchRef and loses persisted supersession lineage.
A prior superseding branch is accepted without canonical reconstruction.
A fresh successor branch is derived from the prior suffix instead of stable root.
A retry pushes over an existing branch instead of reusing exact state.
Supersedes metadata records the wrong predecessor branch.
edgeCases: First supersession from the root canonical branch.
Second or later supersession when persisted branchRef already contains a supersede suffix.
Prior superseding remote has wrong base, tree or commit identity.
Fresh deterministic successor branch already exists and is exact.
Fresh deterministic successor branch exists but has drift.
Materialization is ALREADY_APPLIED and needs no branch.
Main advances multiple times while the same U01 remains STALE.

alternatives.summary: Validate persisted prior branch separately while deriving the next branch from the stable root canonical identity.
alternatives.reason: Preserves lineage, deterministic names and fail-closed validation across repeated supersessions.

alternatives.summary: Keep prior branchRef as the new canonical branch after AUTHORIZE.
alternatives.reason: Would conflate naming root with prior materialization and recursively grow supersede suffixes.

alternatives.summary: Rewrite U01 state back to the root branch before replay.
alternatives.reason: Would bypass resumability proof and mutate canonical execution history.

specialistReviews.finding: The branch parameter currently serves two incompatible roles: canonical naming root and prior remote to validate.
specialistReviews.resolution: Separate those identities while preserving deterministic root naming.

specialistReviews.finding: Allowing any persisted branchRef without reconstructing prior materialization would weaken branch trust.
specialistReviews.resolution: Inspect the persisted branch and validate base/tree/commit identity against reconstructed prior manifest before superseding.

specialistReviews.finding: Repeated main drift is normal for resumable execution and must support supersede-of-supersede state without recursive branch naming.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use root canonical branch for fresh naming and prior state branch for lineage validation.

specialistReviews.finding: Release Unit Execution #144 gives a deterministic live reproduction with exact machine code.
specialistReviews.resolution: Add regression before replaying the same immutable source.

challenge.scenario: Persisted prior branch equals root canonical branch.
challenge.finding: Existing first-supersession path must remain unchanged.
challenge.resolution: Use prior branch for validation and root for naming; they coincide in this case.

challenge.scenario: Persisted prior branch is an older deterministic superseding branch.
challenge.finding: Current code rejects it before validating the actual referenced remote.
challenge.resolution: Inspect priorExecution.executionTransaction.branchRef and reconstruct prior manifest against that branch.

challenge.finding: Deriving from priorBranch recursively lengthens and destabilizes branch identity.
challenge.resolution: Derive new superseding branch from root canonical branch plus fresh target/binding.

challenge.scenario: Prior persisted branch is missing remotely.
challenge.finding: Silently falling back to root could sever lineage.
challenge.resolution: Fail closed with a direct prior-branch-missing machine code when persisted prior differs from root.

challenge.scenario: Prior persisted remote exists but tree/base/message differs from reconstructed prior manifest.
challenge.finding: It may be foreign or mutated.
challenge.resolution: Keep existing remoteMaterializationDrift reconstruction checks fail-closed.

challenge.scenario: Fresh deterministic successor branch already exists exactly.
challenge.finding: Retry must not push or create another identity.

challenge.scenario: Fresh deterministic successor exists with drift.
challenge.resolution: Keep exact remote drift failure and prohibit force-push.

challenge.finding: No branch lineage mutation is needed.

proofPlan: Commit this plan only and require Plan Before Code PASS before implementation.
Implement separate persisted-prior branch validation and stable-root successor naming without state edits.
Add regressions for first supersession, supersede-of-supersede resume, exact retry reuse and drift/missing fail-closed behavior.
Require exact-head Knowledge/Plan/Edit-Time/Incremental Replay/Release Risk/full tests/typecheck/build/Completion Truth/Lifecycle PASS.
Merge only on exact-head proof, then rerun immutable source CI 65e52ffd and follow Release Unit Execution through U01.

requirements.requirement: Release-unit branch reconciliation must resume from a validated persisted superseding branch while preserving deterministic successor identity and fail-closed remote validation.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A persisted prior superseding branch may not be trusted without canonical reconstruction and remote identity validation.
Repeated supersession may not recursively derive branch names from earlier supersede suffixes.

requirements.requirement: Resumed materialization must remain bound to exact current main, immutable source identity and canonical Release Risk without force-push or duplicate merge.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A resumed unit may not use an obsolete main lease or overwrite an existing materialization branch.
